questions.text: The term latency refers to a delay that can be experienced in packet-switched networks.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: False.

Student note: Keep the marked answer for this exact paper. In general networking usage, latency is commonly described as delay, so this item is source-specific and should not be silently 'corrected' in the app.

study.title: Latency in packet-switched networks
study.simple: Latency normally means the time delay between sending data and the data being received or acted on.
whyCorrect: The uploaded assessment review marks this statement False, so False must remain the scoring answer for this exact paper. However, standard networking terminology normally does define latency as delay, so this is a source-key anomaly rather than a concept you should learn incorrectly.
notes: Packet-switched data may be delayed by propagation, transmission, processing and queuing.
Lower latency means less delay; bandwidth is how much data can be carried, which is a different idea.
study.pitfall: Do not rewrite the paper's marked answer, but do not memorise 'latency is not delay' as a networking rule.
study.remember: For the paper: False. For the concept: latency = delay.

keyTerms.meaning: Latency normally means the time delay between sending data and the data being received or acted on.

questions.text: Which of the following are central directories that list all domain names currently in use for specific domains?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: root servers.

Student note: For this paper, remember the answer as root servers.

study.title: DNS root servers
study.simple: DNS is a hierarchical naming system that translates domain names into information such as IP addresses.
whyCorrect: The marked answer is root servers. Root servers sit at the top of the DNS hierarchy and direct resolvers toward the correct top-level-domain name servers, so they are central to locating domain information.
notes: DNS hierarchy: root → top-level domain such as .com or .za → authoritative name server for the domain.
Root servers do not store every website's full DNS record; they mainly point queries to the next level.
study.pitfall: The wording 'central directories that list all domain names' is simplified; learn the DNS hierarchy rather than imagining one giant domain list.
study.remember: Root servers are the starting point at the top of DNS.

keyTerms.meaning: DNS is a hierarchical naming system that translates domain names into information such as IP addresses.

questions.text: Which of the following is rarely used today, due to security concerns.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: Telnet.

Student note: Telnet sends traffic without the protection normally expected from modern secure remote-access tools.

study.title: Telnet and secure remote access
study.simple: Telnet is an old remote-terminal protocol that sends session data without modern transport encryption.
whyCorrect: Telnet is rarely chosen for Internet-based administration because usernames, passwords and commands can be exposed in readable form. SSH provides encrypted remote access and largely replaced Telnet for administration.
notes: Telnet commonly uses TCP port 23; SSH commonly uses TCP port 22.
Encryption protects confidentiality and helps prevent credentials being read in transit.
study.pitfall: Do not confuse Telnet with SSH: they can provide similar remote-login use cases, but their security is very different.
study.remember: Remote administration: prefer SSH over plaintext Telnet.

keyTerms.meaning: Telnet is an old remote-terminal protocol that sends session data without modern transport encryption.

questions.text: Which of the following is the core communications protocol for the Internet?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: TCP/IP.

Student note: TCP/IP is the protocol suite used for Internet communication.

study.title: TCP/IP protocol suite
study.simple: TCP/IP is the family of protocols that underpins communication across the Internet.
whyCorrect: The Internet is built around the TCP/IP suite: IP handles addressing and routing between networks, while transport protocols such as TCP or UDP carry application data. Therefore TCP/IP is the core communications protocol suite.
notes: IP moves packets between network addresses.
TCP provides reliable ordered delivery; UDP offers lighter connectionless delivery.
study.pitfall: TCP/IP is a suite, not one single protocol doing every networking job.
study.remember: Internet communication is organised around the TCP/IP suite.

keyTerms.meaning: TCP/IP is the family of protocols that underpins communication across the Internet.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an advantage of client/server computing over centralized mainframe computing?
options: It is easy to expand capacity by adding servers and clients.
Each client added to the network increases the network's overall capacity and transmission speeds.
Client/server networks are less vulnerable, in part because the processing load is balanced over many powerful smaller computers rather than concentrated in a single huge computer.
There is less risk that a system will completely malfunction because backup or mirror servers can pick up the slack if one server goes down.
questions.correctAnswer: Each client added to the network increases the network's overall capacity and transmission speeds.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: Each client added to the network increases the network's overall capacity and transmission speeds..

Student note: The marked answer identifies the statement that is not an advantage.

study.title: Client/server versus centralized mainframe computing
study.simple: Client/server computing divides work between client machines and servers rather than placing almost all processing in one central mainframe.
whyCorrect: Adding a client creates more demand; it does not automatically increase the network's transmission capacity or speed. Therefore that statement is not a genuine client/server advantage.
notes: Advantages can include distributed processing, flexibility and using client resources.
Network capacity depends on links, switches, routers and server/network design—not simply on adding clients.
study.pitfall: The word 'not' changes the task: choose the claimed advantage that is actually false.
study.remember: More clients do not magically make the network faster.

keyTerms.meaning: Client/server computing divides work between client machines and servers rather than placing almost all processing in one central mainframe.

whyCorrect: The course statement is True: systems that are expensive or complex to develop generally also create substantial ongoing maintenance effort, so maintenance cost tends to track development complexity/cost.
notes: Maintenance continues throughout the operational life of the system.
Poor design and technical debt can make maintenance disproportionately expensive.
study.pitfall: Do not think cost ends at launch; lifecycle cost includes operation and maintenance.
study.remember: Development decisions affect long-term maintenance cost.

keyTerms.meaning: Maintenance includes correcting faults, adapting to changed environments and improving a system after it has been delivered.

questions.text: Upgrading a server from a single processor to multiple processors is an example of scaling a site vertically.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: True.

Student note: Vertical scaling means increasing the power or resources of the existing server.

study.title: Vertical scaling
study.simple: Vertical scaling means making one existing machine more powerful.
whyCorrect: Changing a server from one processor to multiple processors adds resources to the same server, so it is a classic scale-up/vertical-scaling example.
notes: Vertical scaling: more CPU, RAM or storage in one machine.
Horizontal scaling: add more machines/nodes and distribute the workload.
study.pitfall: Remember 'up' = stronger server; 'out' = more servers.
study.remember: Multiple processors in one server = vertical scaling.

keyTerms.meaning: Vertical scaling means making one existing machine more powerful.

questions.text: The primary way a website is able to personalize the content presented to a visitor is through the use of:
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: cookies..

Student note: Cookies can store or connect visitor/session information used for personalization.

study.title: Cookies and personalization
study.simple: A cookie is small data associated with a website and stored by the browser, often carrying a session identifier or preferences.
whyCorrect: Cookies let a site recognise a returning browser/session and connect it with stored preferences or behaviour, making personalised content possible.
notes: A cookie may hold an identifier rather than all personal data itself.
Sites can use sessions, accounts and server-side databases together with cookies.
study.pitfall: Cookies are not executable programs by themselves and should not be confused with browser cache files.
study.remember: Cookies help a site remember/recognise a visitor.

keyTerms.meaning: A cookie is small data associated with a website and stored by the browser, often carrying a session identifier or preferences.

questions.text: The web server software used has a significant impact on how a website's web pages look on a user's computer.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: False.

Student note: The paper marks this False; page appearance is mainly determined by the delivered page content, styles and browser rendering rather than the brand of web-server software.

study.title: Web server versus page appearance
study.simple: A web server receives requests and sends web resources; the browser renders HTML, CSS and other front-end content.
whyCorrect: The statement is False because the brand of web-server software does not by itself decide how the page looks. Appearance is mainly determined by the content/styles/scripts delivered and how the browser renders them.
notes: Apache, Nginx or another server can often deliver the same HTML/CSS.
CSS is the main technology used to control presentation and layout.
study.pitfall: Server software matters for performance/configuration, but not directly for visual design.
study.remember: Browser + HTML/CSS determine appearance more directly.

keyTerms.meaning: A web server receives requests and sends web resources; the browser renders HTML, CSS and other front-end content.

questions.text: Which of the following basic system functionalities is used to display goods on a website?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: digital catalog.

Student note: The digital catalog is the customer-facing function used to present products.

study.title: Digital catalog
study.simple: A digital catalog is the e-commerce function that presents products or services with information such as names, descriptions, images and prices.
whyCorrect: Because the requirement is to display goods on a website, the digital catalog is the direct customer-facing system function that meets it.
notes: A shopping cart stores selected items; a catalog presents items available for selection.
Good catalogs often support categories, search, filtering and product details.
study.pitfall: Do not confuse displaying products with processing payment or storing customer accounts.
study.remember: Catalog = show the goods.

keyTerms.meaning: A digital catalog is the e-commerce function that presents products or services with information such as names, descriptions, images and prices.

questions.text: Which of the following is a server-side technique that detects the attributes of the device making the request, and using predefined templates, loads a version of a site optimized for the device?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: AWD.

Student note: The marked answer is AWD, referring here to adaptive web delivery.

study.title: Adaptive Web Design / Delivery
study.simple: Adaptive delivery chooses a suitable predesigned layout or template based on detected device characteristics.
whyCorrect: The marked answer AWD fits because the question describes server-side detection of a requesting device followed by delivery of a device-optimised template, which is the adaptive approach.
notes: Adaptive design uses defined layouts/templates for device classes.
Responsive design usually relies more on flexible client-side layout/CSS that adapts within one design.
study.pitfall: Do not use AWD and responsive design as exact synonyms in this course.
study.remember: Device detected → matching template delivered = adaptive.

keyTerms.meaning: Adaptive delivery chooses a suitable predesigned layout or template based on detected device characteristics.

questions.text: What are the two most important management challenges in building a successful e-commerce presence?
options: developing a clear understanding of business objectives and knowing how to choose the right technology to achieve those objectives
having an accurate understanding of your business environment and an achievable business plan
building a team with the right skill sets and closely managing the development process
identifying the key components of your business plan and selecting the right software, hardware, and infrastructure for your site
questions.correctAnswer: developing a clear understanding of business objectives and knowing how to choose the right technology to achieve those objectives
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: developing a clear understanding of business objectives and knowing how to choose the right technology to achieve those objectives.

Student note: Link the business objective first, then choose technology that supports it.

study.title: Business objectives before technology
study.simple: An e-commerce presence should be designed to achieve defined business goals rather than to use technology simply because it is available.
whyCorrect: The answer identifies the two linked management tasks: first know what the business is trying to achieve, then choose technology that can deliver those objectives within constraints.
notes: Business objectives might include increasing sales, reducing service cost or improving customer retention.
Technology selection should consider capability, cost, skills, security, scalability and maintainability.
study.pitfall: Starting with a fashionable technology and searching for a business purpose afterwards reverses the logic.
study.remember: Objective first, technology second.

keyTerms.meaning: An e-commerce presence should be designed to achieve defined business goals rather than to use technology simply because it is available.

questions.text: Which of the following cannot be used to retrieve objects from a database?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: HTML.

Student note: HTML structures page content; the other listed technologies can participate in server-side database retrieval.

study.title: HTML versus database access
study.simple: HTML is a markup language used to structure content displayed in a web page.
whyCorrect: HTML by itself does not execute database queries or retrieve database objects. Server-side technologies or application code perform database access and then generate HTML for the browser.
notes: Typical database access happens in server-side application code using SQL or data-access libraries.
HTML describes headings, forms, tables, links and other page structure.
study.pitfall: A form written in HTML can collect input, but backend code is still needed to query the database.
study.remember: HTML structures pages; backend code retrieves database data.

keyTerms.meaning: HTML is a markup language used to structure content displayed in a web page.

questions.text: All of the following are basic information requirements for a product database except:
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: customer ID numbers..

Student note: Customer IDs belong to customer data rather than the core product record.

study.title: Product database information
study.simple: A product database stores attributes that describe products being sold.
whyCorrect: Customer ID numbers identify customers, not products, so they do not belong to the basic information requirements of the product database. Product records instead need fields such as product ID, description, price and inventory-related data.
notes: Separate entities/tables reduce mixing unrelated customer and product information.
Relationships such as orders can connect customers to products without putting customer IDs into every product record.
study.pitfall: Ask 'what does this field describe?' to decide which database entity it belongs to.
study.remember: Customer ID → customer data, not product master data.

keyTerms.meaning: A product database stores attributes that describe products being sold.

questions.text: Which of the following types of e-commerce presence is best suited for creating an ongoing conversation with one's customers?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: social media.

Student note: Social media is designed for ongoing two-way interaction and conversation.

study.title: Social media presence
study.simple: Social media platforms are designed around ongoing publishing, responses, comments, sharing and community interaction.
whyCorrect: Because the goal is an ongoing conversation with customers, social media fits better than a mostly one-way or static presence.
notes: Two-way engagement can support service, feedback and community building.
A website may also support interaction, but social platforms are specifically built around continuous social exchange.
study.pitfall: Conversation means interaction over time, not merely publishing advertisements.
study.remember: Ongoing customer conversation → social media.

keyTerms.meaning: Social media platforms are designed around ongoing publishing, responses, comments, sharing and community interaction.

questions.text: Which of the following is the preferred method of implementing a service-oriented architecture?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: web services.

Student note: The assessment links service-oriented architecture implementation with web services.

study.title: Service-oriented architecture and web services
study.simple: SOA structures software as reusable services with clear interfaces that other systems can call.
whyCorrect: Web services are a standard way to expose interoperable service interfaces over networks, so the course identifies them as the preferred implementation method for SOA.
notes: Services reduce tight coupling by exposing defined contracts/interfaces.
Web-service technologies may use REST/HTTP, SOAP or other service mechanisms depending on architecture.
study.pitfall: SOA is the architectural idea; web services are an implementation approach.
study.remember: SOA can be implemented through web services.

keyTerms.meaning: SOA structures software as reusable services with clear interfaces that other systems can call.

questions.text: Which of the following is the preferred method of implementing a service-oriented architecture?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: web services.

Student note: This repeats Question 41; the marked answer is web services.

study.title: Service-oriented architecture and web services
study.simple: SOA organises capabilities as reusable network-accessible services.
whyCorrect: This is a duplicate of Question 41. The marked answer is again web services because they provide a common way to expose and consume service interfaces.
notes: Keep architecture and implementation distinct: SOA is the style, web services are a common mechanism.
Reusable services can be composed into larger business processes.
study.pitfall: Duplicate question, same concept and same answer.
study.remember: SOA → commonly implemented with web services.

keyTerms.meaning: SOA organises capabilities as reusable network-accessible services.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about mobile websites is not true?
options: Mobile websites run on a firm's servers, just like a traditional website.
Mobile websites can be built using standard web tools such as server-side HTML, Linux, PHP and SQL.
Generally, mobile websites operate more quickly than traditional websites viewed on a desktop computer connected to a broadband office network.
Most large firms today have mobile websites.
questions.correctAnswer: Generally, mobile websites operate more quickly than traditional websites viewed on a desktop computer connected to a broadband office network.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: Generally, mobile websites operate more quickly than traditional websites viewed on a desktop computer connected to a broadband office network..

Student note: Because the question asks what is not true, choose the third statement.

study.title: Mobile website performance
study.simple: Mobile-site performance depends on device capability, network quality, page weight and optimisation.
whyCorrect: The claim that mobile websites generally operate faster than traditional sites on a desktop connected to a broadband office network is the statement marked not true. Mobile networks/devices can introduce constraints that make performance slower unless the site is carefully optimised.
notes: Mobile design often reduces asset size and complexity to compensate for device/network limits.
A smaller mobile page can be efficient, but that does not mean mobile is inherently faster than broadband desktop access.
study.pitfall: The question asks for 'not true'; do not select a real mobile-design benefit by mistake.
study.remember: Mobile optimisation helps performance; mobile is not automatically faster.

keyTerms.meaning: Mobile-site performance depends on device capability, network quality, page weight and optimisation.

questions.text: Which of the following cannot be used to retrieve objects from a database?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: HTML.

Student note: This repeats Question 38; the marked answer is HTML.

study.title: HTML versus database access
study.simple: HTML defines page structure but does not itself perform database queries.
whyCorrect: This repeats Question 38. HTML cannot directly retrieve database objects; server-side application logic performs the query and returns results to the page.
notes: Database access typically uses SQL through backend code.
HTML can display returned data once the application has generated the page.
study.pitfall: Do not confuse displaying database results with retrieving them.
study.remember: HTML is presentation/structure, not database query logic.

keyTerms.meaning: HTML defines page structure but does not itself perform database queries.

questions.text: Objects can be retrieved from a database using Java Server Pages.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: True.

Student note: JSP can be used in a server-side Java web application that retrieves data from a database.

study.title: Java Server Pages and database-backed sites
study.simple: JSP is a server-side Java technology used to generate dynamic web content.
whyCorrect: A JSP-based application can execute server-side Java code that communicates with a database, retrieve records and use them to generate the response, so the statement is True.
notes: In well-designed applications, database logic is often placed in separate classes/services rather than directly inside the page.
The important point is that JSP executes on the server, unlike plain static HTML.
study.pitfall: JSP can participate in database retrieval; HTML alone cannot query a database.
study.remember: JSP = server-side Java web technology.

keyTerms.term: Java Server Pages and database-backed sites
keyTerms.meaning: JSP is a server-side Java technology used to generate dynamic web content.

questions.text: All of the following are open-source programming or scripting languages except:
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: ColdFusion.

Student note: Use ColdFusion for this paper. The wording groups technologies broadly, so preserve the source exactly rather than rewriting the options.

study.title: Open-source web technologies
study.simple: Open-source technologies make source code available under licences that permit defined forms of use, inspection, modification and redistribution.
whyCorrect: The course marks ColdFusion as the exception. In this textbook classification, ColdFusion is treated as a proprietary Adobe server-side platform/language environment rather than one of the listed open-source languages.
notes: PHP, Python and similar languages commonly have open-source implementations/ecosystems.
Technology ownership/licensing can be more nuanced than a simple product name, so follow the course classification for the exam.
study.pitfall: Do not generalise from the word 'language' alone; this is a licensing/classification question.
study.remember: For this paper: ColdFusion is the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Open-source technologies make source code available under licences that permit defined forms of use, inspection, modification and redistribution.

questions.text: Which of the following types of sites typically require a high percentage of secure pages?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: trading.

Student note: Trading sites handle sensitive transactions and therefore need many secure pages.

study.title: Secure pages for trading sites
study.simple: Trading sites handle high-value and sensitive operations such as account access, orders, financial data and transactions.
whyCorrect: Because much of the user journey involves sensitive authenticated or transactional data, trading sites require a high proportion of pages to use secure encrypted connections.
notes: HTTPS protects data in transit and authenticates the server certificate identity.
Security also needs authentication, authorisation and secure server-side design; HTTPS alone is not enough.
study.pitfall: A secure page is about protecting the connection and transaction, not merely showing a padlock graphic.
study.remember: Sensitive trading activity demands extensive secure pages.

keyTerms.meaning: Trading sites handle high-value and sensitive operations such as account access, orders, financial data and transactions.

questions.text: The current versions of most web browsers no longer support Java applets.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: True.

Student note: Modern mainstream browsers no longer provide the old Java applet plug-in support.

study.title: Java applets in modern browsers
study.simple: Java applets were small Java programs embedded in web pages through browser plug-in technology.
whyCorrect: The statement is True because mainstream browsers removed the old plug-in mechanisms required to run Java applets, making them effectively unsupported in current browser versions.
notes: Modern web apps use HTML5, JavaScript and Web APIs instead of Java applets.
Java as a server/desktop language still exists; it is specifically browser applet support that disappeared.
study.pitfall: Do not conclude that 'Java is obsolete'; only the applet/browser model is being discussed.
study.remember: Modern browsers no longer support classic Java applets.

keyTerms.meaning: Java applets were small Java programs embedded in web pages through browser plug-in technology.

questions.text: Dynamic page generation enables price discrimination.
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: True.

Student note: Dynamic pages can vary displayed offers or prices based on rules or information available to the site.

study.title: Dynamic pages and price discrimination
study.simple: Dynamic page generation creates page content at request time using data and business rules.
whyCorrect: A site can generate different offers or prices for different users, segments, times or conditions, so dynamic generation can technically enable price discrimination.
notes: Personalisation uses data/rules to vary what different visitors see.
Price discrimination means charging different prices to different buyers or segments for comparable offerings under defined conditions.
study.pitfall: Dynamic generation enables the capability; whether it is lawful or ethical depends on context and implementation.
study.remember: Dynamic content can vary prices by rule or segment.

keyTerms.meaning: Dynamic page generation creates page content at request time using data and business rules.

questions.text: Which of the following typically includes a data flow diagram to describe the flow of information for an e-commerce site?
questions.explanation:
Marked answer from the uploaded 2026 Assessment 2 review: logical design.

Student note: This repeats Question 26; the marked answer is logical design.

study.title: Logical design and data-flow diagrams
study.simple: Logical design models what information a system needs and how it flows between processes, stores and external entities.
whyCorrect: This repeats Question 26. A data flow diagram is used during logical design because it describes information movement without requiring a particular technical implementation.
notes: Logical design focuses on requirements/processes; physical design chooses implementation technology.
DFDs show flows, processes, data stores and external entities.
study.pitfall: Do not confuse a data-flow diagram with a physical network topology.
study.remember: DFD → logical design.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical design models what information a system needs and how it flows between processes, stores and external entities.
